answer: One trellis post carries an anemometer; each claimant locks a 70-credit bond and registers the post serial. Each epoch the claimant posts a signal giving the mean zephyr speed there. Auditors check it against the station table; an error over 1.5 metres per second, or a reused serial, burns the bond and voids the identity. Fees rise: first 32, kth 32+7(k-1), 1000th 7025, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,528,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-anemometer ring fails: a rented sensor bears its owner's serial, so a second key burns both bonds. An honest operator pays 102 once and recovers the bond after audit.
